transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess the main thing bringing me in is that I've just... stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to. 

My fishing gear is just sitting untouched out in the garage, and going out to the woodshop just feels like a chore now. Even with my family, like when my kids try to get me to sit down and play chess with them... I realize I'm really just going through the motions. I just don't have any interest in things anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been... about a year and seven months now. It really started back when my wife’s health problems began, which just kind of changed everything at home.
During this past year and seven months, have there been any periods of a few weeks or longer where you felt significantly worse than you feel right now?

No, not really. I mean, it hasn't really fluctuated much. It's just been... pretty consistently bad this whole time. I haven't noticed any specific weeks where it was significantly worse than it is right now. It's just been a steady kind of low since it all started.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or how much you've been eating since this started?

Yeah, I have. Most days, food just tastes like cardboard to me now. I usually end up skipping breakfast entirely, and even if I've been out on a job site walking around all day, I really just pick at my dinner. Because of that, I've definitely lost some weight without trying to. I've had to bring my belt in a couple of notches lately just to keep my pants up.
Do you find yourself feeling down on yourself or thinking that you're inadequate or a failure?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep thinking I've failed my wife, and my kids, and the guys at work. It feels like if anything goes wrong at all—like a missed appointment, a cost overrun on a job, or a safety issue on the site—I just take it as proof that I'm useless. I really think everyone would be better off without me in charge of things.
How has your sleep been over this past year and seven months?

Honestly, it hasn't been good. I can get into bed completely exhausted, but I just... I either lie there running through bills and job schedules in my head, or I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. Once I'm awake, I can't really get back to sleep. I just stare at the ceiling until it’s time to get up and drive to the site.
Do you find yourself feeling physically drained or lacking in energy throughout the day, even when you haven't been doing much?

Yeah, definitely. It's... well, by midmorning I feel like I’ve already worked a full shift. It doesn't even take a lot of physical work to wipe me out anymore. Just walking the project or climbing a few flights of stairs with the crew, it feels like my body is carrying around wet concrete. I'm just completely drained.
During this year and seven months, have there ever been any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt completely like your old self, free of these symptoms?

No, I don't think so. It's... it's really just been pretty constant this whole time. I mean, maybe I'll have a day or two where things don't feel quite as heavy, but... definitely nothing like two whole months. I honestly haven't felt like my old self in a long time.
Have you ever felt so low that you have had thoughts about ending your life?

Yeah... I have. It's mostly on those early drives to the site, before anyone else is even awake. I just... I catch myself thinking that it would be a lot easier if I just didn't make it there. Sometimes the thought of just steering off the road crosses my mind, and... honestly, it scares me, because it feels a little too close.

When you look back at these past 19 months, would you say that for the majority of the time, your mood has been so low that you have felt completely unable to function or enjoy anything at all, rather than just feeling generally down or 'blah'?

No, I wouldn't say I've been completely unable to function. I mean, I still get up and drive to the site, and I still do my job. It's definitely a lot worse than just feeling 'blah'—it's a really heavy feeling—but I haven't just stopped doing everything. I still get through the day, even if I'm just going through the motions.
